name: Stonewall via the Queen's Gambit
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nf3 c6 g3 f5 Bg2 Nf6 O-O Bd6 b3 O-O
videoTitle: Learn the Stonewall Defense & Attack | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Put the four pawns on d5, e6, c6 and f5 first, before White can break with e4, then develop the knight to f6 (to guard the king), the bishop to d6, and castle. The dream is a knight on e4 and a rook swung up to attack the kingside.
note: Video gives the pawn order and piece plan; White's g3/Bg2/b3 are the masters' most-played moves.

name: Stonewall vs 1.c4: ...e6 then ...d5
moves: c4 e6 Nc3 d5 d4 c6 Nf3 f5
videoTitle: Learn the Stonewall Defense & Attack | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against the English, start with ...e6 and ...d5 so White can't stop the setup, then add ...c6 and ...f5 to reach the same Stonewall wall.
note: White's moves are the masters' most-played; the video says to meet 1.c4 with ...e6 then ...d5.

name: QGA vs 3.e4: strike back with ...e5
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 e5 Nf3 exd4
videoTitle: STOP PLAYING These 4 Chess Openings
idea: If you do accept the gambit, you can't let White build e4-d4 for free. Hitting the centre at once with ...e5 and taking on d4 keeps White from rolling forward.
note: Levy advises against 2...dxc4 for most club players, but says this is what to do if you take it; Nf3 exd4 are the masters' most-played moves.

name: QGA vs 3.e4: ...Nf6 and the d5 blockade
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Bxc4 Nb6
videoTitle: STOP PLAYING These 4 Chess Openings
idea: The other way to fight the centre: ...Nf6 hits e4, and when the pawn advances the knight sits on d5 as a blockader before dropping back to b6 to hit the c4 bishop.
note: Video shows ...Nf6, e5, ...Nd5; Bxc4 Nb6 are the masters' most-played continuation.

name: QGA trap: holding the pawn with ...b5 loses the rook
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 c6 axb5 cxb5 Qf3
videoTitle: STOP PLAYING These 4 Chess Openings
idea: The warning line: clinging to the extra pawn with ...b5 and ...c6 opens the long diagonal, and Qf3 hits the a8 rook. Black has to give up material to block, which is why the pawn is not really free.

name: Leningrad Dutch vs the London
moves: d4 f5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 g6 Nf3 Bg7
videoTitle: HOW TO WIN AT CHESS!!!!!!!
idea: The Dutch is a good practical answer to the London: Black fianchettoes as usual and aims for an ...e5 break that the London setup finds uncomfortable. The one aggressive try to know is White's h-pawn push to hit the g6 'hook' in front of the king.

name: Slav ...Bf5 vs the Nh4 sortie
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 Nc3 e6 Nh4 Bg6 Nxg6 hxg6
videoTitle: CHESS STEPS #4 (1400-1600)
idea: With the bishop outside the pawn chain, White has two ways to punish it: Qb3 against b7, and the knight jump to h4 to win the bishop pair. Retreating to g6 means that if the knight takes, Black recaptures toward the centre and gets a half-open h-file in return.
note: Video names Qb3 and the Nh4 sortie as the punishers of an early ...Bf5; ...Bg6 Nxg6 hxg6 is the masters' most-played continuation.

name: Leningrad Dutch: ...d6 and ...Nc6
moves: d4 f5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 g6 Nf3 Bg7 O-O O-O c4 d6 Nc3 Nc6
videoTitle: BEST Chess Openings by Elo
idea: Recommended against any first move but 1.e4: a reversed Sicilian. After the fianchetto and ...d6, the knight comes to c6 (or d7 with ...Qe8) to support the ...e5 push, and Black can then storm the kingside as in a Closed Sicilian.
note: Video names ...d6, ...Nc6 or ...Nd7 and ...Qe8 to push ...e5; White's moves are the masters' main line.

name: Anti-London: 2...c5 and the rare ...f6
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6 c3 f6 Nd2 e5
videoTitle: Want To Crush The London System?
idea: Hit the London at once with ...c5, swap on d4 and bring the knight to c6. Then, instead of ...Nf6, the f-pawn goes to f6 so Black can play ...e5, taking the centre away from White and knocking the f4 bishop around.

name: Anti-London vs 6.Nf3: ...g5 and ...h5
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6 c3 f6 Nf3 g5 Bg3 h5 h4 g4
videoTitle: Want To Crush The London System?
idea: If White's knight covers e5, Black grabs kingside space with ...g5 and ...h5 instead; after h4 the pawn on g4 kicks the f3 knight out of the centre and Black has a big space edge. Early Qh5+ checks look scary but ...g6 usually handles them.

name: Anti-London vs 6.Bd3: ...e5 and the Qh5+ trick
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6 c3 f6 Bd3 e5 Qh5+ g6 Bxg6+ hxg6 Qxh8 exf4
videoTitle: Want To Crush The London System?
idea: ...e5 is still playable after Bd3. The check on h5 looks deadly because ...g6 seems to drop to Bxg6+, but after the bishop takes and the queen grabs the h8 rook, ...exf4 wins the London bishop and White's queen is stranded; with the e-file open, ...Qe7+ and long castling follow.

name: Anti-London: 3.dxc5 Nc6 and ...e5
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 c5 dxc5 Nc6 e3 e5 Bg3 Bxc5
videoTitle: Want To Crush The London System?
idea: Taking on c5 gives up the centre: Black develops the knight, adds a second central pawn with ...e5 that kicks the bishop, and simply wins the c5 pawn back with a fine game.

name: Anti-London via 2.Nf3 Nc6: ...Bg4 and ...f6
moves: d4 d5 Nf3 Nc6 Bf4 Bg4 e3 f6 c4 e5
videoTitle: Want To Crush The London System?
idea: After 2.Nf3 the knight goes to c6, and when the bishop comes to f4 the other bishop pins the f3 knight; ...f6 and ...e5 then challenge the centre with the knight on f3 unable to help.
note: Video's training game; Levy notes ...e6/...Bd6 is the more accurate order but shows this one for practicality.

name: Beefeater: ...Bxc3+ and ...f5
moves: d4 g6 c4 Bg7 Nc3 c5 d5 Bxc3+ bxc3 f5 Nf3 Nf6
videoTitle: THE BEEF EATER | Epic Opening for Black
idea: Black gives up the g7 bishop to wreck White's pawns: c3 and c4 are left doubled and frozen. The f-pawn and the f6 knight fight for e4, and the plan is ...d6, ...Qa5 hitting c3, ...Nd7, then choose between ...Ne4 in the centre, ...h6/...g5 on the kingside or ...b5 on the queenside.

name: Beefeater vs 6.e4: ...e5 after 7.f3
moves: d4 g6 c4 Bg7 Nc3 c5 d5 Bxc3+ bxc3 f5 e4 fxe4 f3 e5 dxe6 Nc6 exd7+ Bxd7
videoTitle: THE BEEF EATER | Epic Opening for Black
idea: The critical try: White gambits for a pawn front. Black answers f3 with ...e5, and after the en-passant capture develops with ...Nc6 and ...Bxd7. White still can't take on e4 because ...Qh4+ hits the pawn, and Black follows with ...Qe7 and long castling while White has no pieces out.

name: Beefeater vs 6.h4: ...Qa5
moves: d4 g6 c4 Bg7 Nc3 c5 d5 Bxc3+ bxc3 f5 h4 Qa5 Qc2 Nf6
videoTitle: THE BEEF EATER | Epic Opening for Black
idea: Against the h-pawn push Black doesn't panic: the queen still attacks the weak c3 pawn and the knight comes to f6. If White plays h5, taking it is fine because the queen can't use f5 while c3 is hanging.

name: Beefeater move order via 3.Nf3 c5 4.d5 f5
moves: d4 g6 c4 Bg7 Nf3 c5 d5 f5 Nc3 Bxc3+ bxc3
videoTitle: THE BEEF EATER | Epic Opening for Black
idea: If White develops the king's knight first, ...c5 still comes. After d5, ...f5 invites Nc3, and the trade on c3 brings the game straight back into the Beefeater structure.

name: Beefeater: 4.dxc5 Na6
moves: d4 g6 c4 Bg7 Nf3 c5 dxc5 Na6
videoTitle: THE BEEF EATER | Epic Opening for Black
idea: Taking on c5 is a mistake: the knight heads for c5, the queen can come to a5 and the g7 bishop rakes the long diagonal, so White can't hold the extra pawn.

name: Modern into King's Indian: ...Nd7 and a quick ...e5
moves: d4 g6 c4 Bg7 e4 d6 Nc3 Nd7 Nf3 e5 d5 Ne7
videoTitle: THE BEEF EATER | Epic Opening for Black
idea: If White plays e4, Black is in a King's Indian without having committed the knight to f6. That lets ...Nd7 support a fast ...e5, and after d5 the king's knight goes to e7 so ...f5 can come without wasting a tempo; ...h6 keeps pieces off g5.

name: Modern vs the London: ...c5
moves: d4 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3 c5 c3 cxd4 exd4 Nf6
videoTitle: THE BEEF EATER | Epic Opening for Black
idea: Against the London, ...c5 is strong because it opens the long diagonal for the g7 bishop. After the trade on d4 Black develops the knight and follows with ...d5.

name: Albin vs 3.e3: take on d4 and develop
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 e3 exd4 exd4 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4
videoTitle: The Chess GAMBITS Tier List ft. Hikaru Nakamura
idea: If White sidesteps the gambit with e3, there is no pawn to hunt, so Black just trades on d4 and develops fast: knight to f6, bishop pins on b4, then castle and put a rook on e8 against the isolated d-pawn structure.
note: From the gambit tier list recorded with Hikaru.

name: Albin: main tabiya 4.Nf3 Nc6
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3 Nc6
videoTitle: CRUSH The Queen's Gambit in 6 Moves: THE ALBIN
idea: Black answers the Queen's Gambit with a counter-gambit. The pawn on d4 wedges into White's position, takes e3 and c3 from White's pieces, and the knight on c6 starts the plan of winning back the e5 pawn.

name: Lasker Trap: underpromote to a knight
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 e3 Bb4+ Bd2 dxe3 Bxb4 exf2+ Ke2 fxg1=N+ Rxg1 Bg4+
videoTitle: CRUSH The Queen's Gambit in 6 Moves: THE ALBIN
idea: If White plays e3 too early, the check on b4 comes first and then the pawn runs down to f2 and g1. Promoting to a knight with check is the key: after the rook recaptures, the bishop check from g4 skewers the king to the queen on d1.

name: Lasker Trap: 8.Ke1 Qh4+
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 e3 Bb4+ Bd2 dxe3 Bxb4 exf2+ Ke2 fxg1=N+ Ke1 Qh4+ g3 Qe4+
videoTitle: CRUSH The Queen's Gambit in 6 Moves: THE ALBIN
idea: If the king steps back instead of taking the new knight, the queen checks from h4 and then from e4, forking king and the h1 rook.

name: Albin vs 5.a3: the ...f6 double gambit
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3 Nc6 a3 f6 exf6 Nxf6
videoTitle: CRUSH The Queen's Gambit in 6 Moves: THE ALBIN
idea: When White spends a move on a3 to stop ...Bb4, Black offers a second pawn to open lines. After the recapture Black develops fast, uses ...a5 to stop b4, and builds a queen-and-bishop battery toward h3.

name: Albin vs 5.a3: ...a5 and the knight to g6
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3 Nc6 a3 a5 g3 Nge7 Bg2 Ng6
videoTitle: CRUSH The Queen's Gambit in 6 Moves: THE ALBIN
idea: A slower route: ...a5 stops b4, then the king's knight goes e7 and g6 to hit the e5 pawn and win the gambit pawn back.
note: White's g3/Bg2 are amateur-database moves; the knight route is from the video.

name: Albin vs 5.a3: ...Bg4 and long castling
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3 Nc6 a3 Bg4 Nbd2 Qe7
videoTitle: CRUSH The Queen's Gambit in 6 Moves: THE ALBIN
idea: The main line: the bishop pins the f3 knight, which defends e5, and the queen steps to e7 to attack e5 and prepare queenside castling.
note: Video gives ...Bg4 then ...Qe7 or ...Qd7 and long castling; Nbd2 and ...Qe7 are the masters' most-played.

name: Albin vs 5.g3: ...Be6, ...Qd7, long castle, ...h5
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3 Nc6 g3 Be6 Nbd2 Qd7 Bg2 O-O-O O-O h5
videoTitle: CRUSH The Queen's Gambit in 6 Moves: THE ALBIN
idea: Against the fianchetto Black doesn't rush to win the pawn back. The bishop eyes c4, the queen and rook line up on the d-file after long castling, and the h-pawn charges at White's king.
note: Plan from the video; White's Nbd2/Bg2/O-O are the masters' most-played.

name: Albin vs 3.Nc3: the d-file mating net
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 Nc3 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qxd5 Be6 Qxd8+ Rxd8
videoTitle: CRUSH The Queen's Gambit in 6 Moves: THE ALBIN
idea: If White develops instead of taking, Black takes on d4 and kicks the queen. Grabbing a second pawn walks into ...Be6, the queens come off, and the rook on the open d-file plus ...Nb4 and ...Nc2 threaten mate.
note: Black is a pawn down after the queen trade (engine about -0.35); the mate threat with ...Nb4 and ...Nc2 is the practical trick.

name: Albin idea via 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.c4 e5
moves: d4 d5 Nf3 Nc6 c4 e5 cxd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Bb4
videoTitle: CRUSH The Queen's Gambit in 6 Moves: THE ALBIN
idea: Against 2.Nf3 the knight goes to c6 first, and 3.c4 still gets ...e5. If White takes on d5 and attacks the queen with the knight, ...Bb4 pins that knight so it cannot capture.

name: Grünfeld Exchange: ...c5 against the big centre
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Nf3 c5
videoTitle: This Opening Will SKYROCKET Your Chess Elo
idea: Black lets White build e4-d4 on purpose, trades knights on c3 and then attacks the centre from a distance: the g7 bishop and ...c5 are the core, with ...Qa5, ...Bg4, ...Nc6 and castling added in whatever order fits.

name: Grünfeld Exchange: 8.Be3 Qa5
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Nf3 c5 Be3 Qa5 Qd2
videoTitle: This Opening Will SKYROCKET Your Chess Elo
idea: When White guards d4 with the bishop, the queen jumps to a5 to hit the weak c3 pawn; White has to defend with Qd2, and Black keeps piling on with ...Bg4, ...Nc6 and ...cxd4.
note: Video plays ...c5, ...Qa5 against the bishop setup; Be3 and Qd2 are the masters' main moves.

name: Grünfeld: 5.Nxd5 Qxd5, the club player's choice
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 Nxd5 Qxd5 Nf3 Bg7 e3 c5
videoTitle: This Opening Will SKYROCKET Your Chess Elo
idea: Many club players trade knights on d5 instead of playing e4. That just helps Black: the queen recaptures centrally, the bishop comes to g7 and ...c5, ...Nc6 and a bishop to g4 or f5 follow with pressure on d4.
note: Video says taking on d5 is the most common intermediate move; White's Nf3/e3 are amateur-database moves.

name: Grünfeld: 4.Nf3 Bg7, wait for the capture
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg7
videoTitle: This Opening Will SKYROCKET Your Chess Elo
idea: If White develops instead of capturing, Black just develops too. Whenever White does take on d5, the same recipe applies: trade on c3, castle, then ...c5, ...Qa5, ...Nc6 and ...Bg4.

name: Grünfeld vs 4.e3: hit the centre with ...c5
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 e3 Bg7 Nf3 c5
videoTitle: This Opening Will SKYROCKET Your Chess Elo
idea: Against a quiet setup that never captures on d5, Black still opens the g7 bishop's diagonal with ...c5, since that bishop is the piece that wins Grünfeld games.

name: Grünfeld Exchange: Bc4 and Ne2 setup
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Bc4 c5 Ne2 Nc6 Be3 O-O
videoTitle: This Opening Will SKYROCKET Your Chess Elo
idea: With the knight on e2 instead of f3, the g4 square is no longer a good target for the bishop, so Black leans on ...c5 and ...Nc6 against d4 and castles; White's f3 can kick a bishop from g4.
note: Video names the Bc4/Ne2 setup and ...c5; ...Nc6 and Be3 O-O are the masters' main moves.

name: Grünfeld setup without Nc3: ...Bg7 and ...c5
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 g3 c5
videoTitle: This Opening Will SKYROCKET Your Chess Elo
idea: If White never puts a knight on c3, rushing ...d5 leaves Black's knight with nothing to trade on c3. Instead Black fianchettoes and uses ...c5 to make the g7 bishop count.

name: Grünfeld ideas vs the English
moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5
videoTitle: This Opening Will SKYROCKET Your Chess Elo
idea: Against 1.c4 the same ...Nf6, ...g6, ...d5 ideas still work: the knight recaptures on d5 and Black follows with ...g6 and ...Bg7 aiming at the long diagonal.
note: Video: knight f6, g6, d5 'still works' vs the English; the move order shown is the masters' most-played route.

name: Budapest: 3...Ng4 tabiya
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: Black gives the e-pawn after 2.c4 and immediately hunts it: the knight on g4 hits e5, ...Nc6 adds a second attacker, and a ...Bb4+ check speeds up development before White can hold on to the pawn.

name: Kieninger Trap: ...Nd3 mate
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Nf3 Nc6 Bf4 Bb4+ Nbd2 Qe7 a3 Ngxe5 axb4 Nd3#
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: With the queen on e7 behind the e5 knight, the e2 pawn is pinned. If White grabs the b4 bishop, the knight jumps to d3 and it is mate because e2 can't capture.
note: ends in mate; database counts are for the position before the mating move

name: Budapest: the in-between ...Bxd2+
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Nf3 Nc6 Bf4 Bb4+ Nbd2 Qe7 a3 Ngxe5 Nxe5 Nxe5 Bxe5 Bxd2+ Qxd2 Qxe5
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: If White sidesteps the mate by trading on e5, don't recapture on e5 at once or the b4 bishop falls to the a3 pawn. Throw in the bishop trade on d2 first, then take back on e5 with an equal game.

name: Budapest Rubinstein: castle, ...a5 and the rook lift
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Bf4 Nc6 Nf3 Bb4+ Nbd2 Qe7 e3 Ngxe5 Nxe5 Nxe5 Be2 O-O O-O a5
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: Black wins the pawn back and castles; then ...a5 gives the a8 rook a path along the sixth rank via a6 to g6 for a kingside attack — a gambit that is not objectively lost.
note: Video gives castling, ...a5 and the ...Ra6-g6 lift; the move order to get there is the masters' main line.

name: Reverse Smith-Morra vs 1.c4
moves: c4 e5 g3 d5 cxd5 c6
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: An offbeat try against the English: Black offers the c-pawn the way White does in the Smith-Morra, hoping for fast development and active squares. The engine does not like it, so treat it as a surprise weapon.
note: Levy presents it as an idea he says the engine dislikes.

name: 1.Nf3 g5: Herrström Gambit
moves: Nf3 g5 Nxg5 e5
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: A blitz surprise: the g-pawn is offered, and once White takes, ...e5 opens the queen's diagonal toward the g5 knight and claims the centre. Levy calls it silly but fun.

name: Slav: three-knights tabiya
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3
videoTitle: Learn the Slav Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The c-pawn backs up d5 so Black keeps the centre without locking in the light-squared bishop. With both sets of knights out, Black now picks a structure: grab c4, build the e6 triangle, prepare ...b5 with ...a6, or fianchetto.

name: Open Slav: 5.a4 main line
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O O-O
videoTitle: Learn the Slav Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Black takes on c4 only briefly. White's a4 stops ...b5 from holding the pawn, so Black develops the bishop to f5 before ...e6 and castles with a sound structure.
note: Moves after 5.a4 are the masters' most-played continuation; the video names the a4 main line and 'develop naturally'.

name: Open Slav: Geller Gambit 5.e4
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 e4 b5 e5 Nd5
videoTitle: Learn the Slav Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: White ignores the c4 pawn and grabs the centre at once. Black keeps the extra pawn with ...b5 and lands the knight on d5 when it is kicked.
note: The video names 5.e4 as the Geller Gambit; ...b5 e5 Nd5 is the masters' only-played continuation.

name: Semi-Slav: e6 triangle with ...Bd6
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 Bd6 O-O O-O
videoTitle: Learn the Slav Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: A system approach: pawns on c6-d5-e6, knight to d7, bishop to d6 and castle. It is very solid, but White's thematic e4 break at the right moment is the thing to prepare for.

name: Semi-Slav: Cambridge Springs pin
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Bg5 Nbd7 e3 Qa5 Nd2 Bb4 Qc2 O-O
videoTitle: Learn the Slav Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against Bg5 the queen jumps to a5 and the bishop to b4, pinning the c3 knight so ...Ne4 tactics hit the pinned piece and the loose g5 bishop.
note: Video names Qa5 + Bb4 + the pin; White's Nd2/Qc2 are the masters' main replies.

name: Slav vs the Catalan setup (g3)
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 g3 Bf5 Bg2 e6 O-O Nbd7
videoTitle: Learn the Slav Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: When White fianchettoes, Black gets the light bishop out to f5 before ...e6, then follows with ...Nbd7 and ...Bd6 — a London-style setup with the colours reversed.

name: Slav vs 4.e3: watch for Qb3
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 Nc3 e6 Qb3 Qb6
videoTitle: Learn the Slav Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Developing the bishop outside the pawn chain leaves b7 loose, and White's early Qb3 hits it and the centre at once. Black answers by covering b7 with the queen.
note: Video warns about Qb3 hitting b7; ...Qb6 is the masters' most-played answer.

name: Slav vs the English (1.c4 c6)
moves: c4 c6 Nc3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nf3
videoTitle: Learn the Slav Defense | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The same c6-d5 setup works against 1.c4: once White adds d4 the game steers straight back into a main-line Slav.
note: Moves after 2...d5 are the masters' most-played; the video says the English is hard to keep out of the Slav.

name: Anti-London: ...Nf6, ...c5 and ...Qb6 at b2
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c5 c3 Qb6 Qb3 c4 Qc2
videoTitle: CHESS STEPS #3 (1000-1400)
idea: Levy's 'optimal' answer to the London: knight behind the c-pawn, ...c5 for real central pressure, and the queen to b6 eyeing b2 (the London bishop has left the queenside). When White offers the queen trade, ...c4 gains space and chases the queen, and Black follows by developing the light bishop and expanding on the queenside.
note: Move order after 4...Qb6 is the masters' main line.

name: Anti-London spiky setup: ...g5 and ...Nh6-f5
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6 c3 f6 Nf3 g5 Bg3 Nh6 Bd3 Nf5
videoTitle: CHESS STEPS #3 (1000-1400)
idea: An unorthodox route in the ...f6 system: the king's knight goes h6 and f5 to trade itself for the g3 bishop, after which Black plays ...Bg7, castles and aims for ...e5. Levy calls it double-edged and not for the faint of heart.
note: White's Bd3 is the amateur database's most-played; the ...g5, ...Nh6, ...Nf5 route is from the video.

name: KID Classical: close the centre, then ...f5
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5 O-O Nc6 d5 Ne7 Ne1 Nd7 Nd3 f5
videoTitle: Learn the King's Indian Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Fianchetto, castle, strike with ...e5. Once White closes the centre with d5, the knight retreats to d7 so the f-pawn can advance: ...f5 starts the kingside attack, which only works after the centre is locked.
note: Video gives the plan (e5, close the centre, knight to d7, ...f5); the move order is the masters' main line (Mar del Plata).

name: KID vs the London: knight to d7 and ...e5
moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3 d6 h3 O-O Be2 Nfd7 O-O e5
videoTitle: Learn the King's Indian Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: There is no need to trade off the f4 bishop. With the fianchetto in place the f6 knight steps back to d7, uncovering the long diagonal and backing ...e5, which hits the bishop and grabs the centre.
note: Video: 'slide this knight back to d7 once the bishop is out … looking for e5'; White's moves are the masters' most-played.

name: King's Indian vs 1.Nf3 (fianchetto)
moves: Nf3 Nf6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 O-O O-O d4 d6 c4 Nc6
videoTitle: Learn the King's Indian Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The same setup works against anything: fianchetto, castle and ...d6. Against a White fianchetto the knight goes to c6 to back ...e5.
note: Video says the KID setup is playable vs 1.c4 and 1.Nf3; ...Nc6 is the masters' most-played reply here.

name: QGA vs 3.e3: ...e5
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 e5 Bxc4 exd4
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: Levy's choice after accepting against e3: hit the centre with ...e5 straight away. When White recovers the c4 pawn, Black swaps off the d4 pawn and gets free development.

name: QGA vs 3.e3 e5 4.dxe5: early queen trade and ...Bg4+
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 e5 dxe5 Qxd1+ Kxd1 Nc6 Bxc4 Bg4+
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: If White grabs e5 instead, the queens come off with check and the king is stuck on d1. The knight hits e5 and the bishop checks from g4 along the empty d1-h5 diagonal, so Black leads in development and can castle long.
note: White's 6.Bxc4 is the amateur database's most-played; the ...Nc6, ...Bg4+ and long-castle plan is from the video.

name: QGA vs 3.Nf3: ...Nf6, ...Bg4, then ...e6
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bg4 Bxc4 e6
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: With the knight on f3, ...e5 doesn't work. Instead the knight covers e4 and the light bishop gets out before ...e6 shuts it in. The dark bishop and castling come next, but time ...Bb4 carefully: with White's knight on c3, Qa4+ hits the king and the b4 bishop.
note: Video: develop the bishop, ...e6, bishop to b4 and castle. Engine check: ...Bb4 straight after Nc3 loses to Qa4+ (-1.8), so the line stops before it.

name: QGD vs the Catalan: ...Be7, castle, ...b6
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nf3 Nf6 g3 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O b6
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: Against the fianchetto the light bishop can't come out via c8-g4, so it goes to b7 after ...b6; then ...Nbd7 and ...c5 give Black two pawns fighting for the centre.

name: Chigorin: 3.cxd5 Qxd5 4.e3 e5
moves: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 cxd5 Qxd5 e3 e5 Nc3 Bb4 Bd2 Bxc3
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: A Queen's Gambit weapon that develops a knight in front of the c-pawn. After the trade on d5 the queen and knight both hit d4, ...e5 strikes the centre, and when Nc3 attacks the queen Black pins with ...Bb4 instead of moving her, trades on c3, then develops and castles long.

name: Chigorin: 3.cxd5 Qxd5 4.Nc3?! Qxd4
moves: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 cxd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qxd4
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: With queen and knight both hitting d4, attacking the queen with Nc3 straight away just drops the d4 pawn.

name: Chigorin vs 3.Nf3: ...Bg4 at once
moves: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Bxf3 gxf3 Qxd5 e3 e5 Nc3 Bb4
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: White's most solid answer is Nf3, so Black pins it at once with ...Bg4, gives the bishop for the knight to damage White's structure, then plays the same ...Qxd5, ...e5 and ...Bb4 pin.
note: Video: play ...Bg4 as fast as possible; the rest is the masters' main line.

name: QGD classical: ...Nf6, ...Be7, castle vs Bg5
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h6
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: The rock-solid Queen's Gambit Declined: support d5 with the e-pawn, develop the knight and bishop and castle. ...h6 asks the g5 bishop a question; Levy warns that against an early Qc2 setup a careless ...h6 can run into a Bxh6 sacrifice, so watch the h7 pawn.
note: Levy names the setup (…Nf6, …Be7, castle) and White's Bg5/Bf4 main lines; ...h6 is the masters' most-played.

name: Tarrasch Defense: 3...c5
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5 cxd5 exd5 Nf3 Nc6 g3 Nf6 Bg2 Be7 O-O O-O
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: A more active way to decline: Black strikes the centre with ...c5 and accepts an isolated d-pawn in return for free piece play and open lines.
note: Named in the video as the aggressive QGD; the move order is the masters' main line.

name: Ragozin: 4...Bb4
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Bb4
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: Instead of the passive ...Be7, the bishop goes to b4 to pin the c3 knight, a Nimzo-Indian idea inside the Queen's Gambit Declined.
note: Named in the video; moves are standard.

name: Baltic Defense: 2...Bf5 and the ...Nc6-b4 idea
moves: d4 d5 c4 Bf5 Nc3 e6 Nf3 Nc6
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: An aggressive sideline: the light bishop comes out before ...e6 locks it in, and the knight on c6 eyes b4 and c2. Levy's advice to White is to stay solid, so Black needs more than that cheap trick.
note: Levy covers this from White's side; the moves are the masters' main line.

name: Anti-London: 2...Nc6, ...f6, ...Bg4 and ...e5
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nc6 e3 f6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 Bxf3 Bxf3 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Bg3 Nf6 O-O e4
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: A direct central assault: the knight goes in front of the c-pawn on purpose, ...f6 prepares ...e5, and when the f3 knight stops it, the bishop pins and then trades it off. After the swap on e5 Black has two central pawns backed by knights, then gains time on the g3 bishop's partner with ...e4 and can castle long and attack.
note: Moves through 8...Nf6 are from the video; ...e4 after castling is the amateur database's most-played and matches 'now you attack the bishop'.

name: Dutch with ...Bb4 vs the English
moves: c4 f5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 g3 Bb4
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: Levy's easiest Dutch: the bishop goes to b4 to trade itself for the c3 knight, the other bishop fianchettoes on b7, and after castling the knight lands on e4 with a kingside attack built from ...Qf6, ...g5, ...Rf6 and ...Rh6.

name: Nimzo-English: ...Bb4 and ...b6 setup
moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3 Bb4 g3 b6 Bg2 Bb7
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: The same plan reached from 1...Nf6: pin and later take the c3 knight, fianchetto on b7, castle, then put a knight on e4 with ...f5 behind it. If White ever plays a3, take on c3.
note: Levy shows ...Bb4 and the b7 fianchetto against Nc3/Nf3; White's g3/Bg2 are the amateur database's most-played.

name: Leningrad Dutch: ...Qe8 and ...e5
moves: d4 f5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 g6 Nf3 Bg7 O-O O-O c4 d6 Nc3 Qe8
videoTitle: Learn the Dutch Defense Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: A King's Indian setup where the f-pawn is already on f5, so one central lever is in. The queen steps to e8 to support the second one, ...e5, giving Black active central play and kingside attacking chances.
note: Video describes the g6 Leningrad setup and the ...Qe8 / ...e5 plan; White's move order is the masters' main line.

name: Classical Dutch setup
moves: d4 f5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 e6 Nf3 Be7 O-O O-O c4 d6
videoTitle: Learn the Dutch Defense Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The quieter Dutch: bishop to e7, pawns on e6 and d6, castle short. Less committal than the Leningrad, it keeps the f5 grip on e4 and waits for ...e5 later.
note: Video names the classical setup; the move order is the masters' most-played.

name: Staunton Gambit 4.f3: don't take, play ...d5
moves: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 d5 fxe4 dxe4
videoTitle: Learn the Dutch Defense Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Take the first pawn and develop the knight, but do not grab the second one on f3 — that only opens lines toward the king. Instead ...d5 claims the centre and lets White recapture on e4, with Black developing quickly and keeping the position closed around the king.
note: Levy: 'don't take the second pawn, give this pawn back and take the centre'. Recorded as 4...d5, the masters' main move (66 of 87 games) and the engine's choice (~equal). Read literally as 4...e3 (return the pawn) it scores about -1.2 for Black at depth 16.

name: Staunton Gambit 4.Bg5: ...g6 and castle
moves: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 g6
videoTitle: Learn the Dutch Defense Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against the bishop pin the simplest plan is the fianchetto: ...g6, ...Bg7 and castle, after which the pin on f6 stops mattering.

name: Staunton Gambit 4.Bg5: ...c6 then ...d5
moves: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 c6
videoTitle: Learn the Dutch Defense Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: An alternative to ...g6: ...c6 opens the queen's path to b6 and prepares a safely supported ...d5.

name: Staunton trap: the premature ...d5
moves: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 d5 Bxf6 exf6 Qh5+ g6 Qxd5
videoTitle: Learn the Dutch Defense Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The warning line. After ...d5 White removes the f6 knight, and once Black recaptures toward the centre the queen check on h5 forces ...g6 and the queen collects the d5 pawn with a big edge.

name: Dutch vs 1.Nf3: Lisitsin Gambit
moves: Nf3 f5 e4 fxe4 Ng5 Nf6 d3 e5
videoTitle: Learn the Dutch Defense Setup | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The same ...f5 against 1.Nf3 invites the Lisitsin Gambit. Black takes the pawn, develops, and plants a pawn on e5 so the king is not left exposed.
note: Video: 'take and then just solidify in the centre'; the ...e5 move order is the masters' most-played.

name: Nimzo-Indian: 3...Bb4 pin
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4
videoTitle: WIN GAMES with the Nimzo-Indian Defense!
idea: Black fights for the centre with pieces: the bishop pins the c3 knight to the king so White cannot simply play e4. The long-term plan is to take on c3, double White's pawns and fianchetto on b7 with a knight planted on e4.

name: Nimzo vs 4.e3: ...b6, ...Bb7 and ...Ne4
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3 b6 Bd3 Bb7 Nf3 Ne4
videoTitle: WIN GAMES with the Nimzo-Indian Defense!
idea: Instead of castling at once, the recommended practical setup: fianchetto the queen's bishop and jump the knight to e4, ready to glue it there with ...f5 and to take on c3 when it suits Black.
note: White's Bd3/Nf3 are masters' moves (Ne2 is more common there).

name: Nimzo vs 4.e3: castle, ...d5 and ...c5
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3 O-O Bd3 d5 Nf3 c5 O-O
videoTitle: WIN GAMES with the Nimzo-Indian Defense!
idea: The classical main line: castle, then strike the centre with both ...d5 and ...c5 before White's pieces get comfortable.
note: White's Bd3/Nf3/O-O are the masters' most-played.

name: Nimzo vs 4.Qc2: trade on c3, ...Bb7 and ...Ne4
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2 b6 a3 Bxc3+ Qxc3 Bb7 Nf3 Ne4
videoTitle: WIN GAMES with the Nimzo-Indian Defense!
idea: White's queen move aims to recapture on c3 without doubled pawns, but Black still gets the bishop pair trade, the b7 fianchetto and a knight on e4, later supported by ...f5 and ...d6.

name: Nimzo vs 4.Qc2 b6 5.e4: ...c5
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2 b6 e4 c5
videoTitle: WIN GAMES with the Nimzo-Indian Defense!
idea: White's sharpest answer to ...b6 is e4, taking the centre before the bishop reaches b7. Black's main reply is to hit the centre straight away with ...c5 and open the position.

name: Nimzo vs 4.Qc2: ...Nc6 and ...e5 build-up
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2 Nc6 Nf3 d6 a3 Bxc3+ Qxc3 O-O
videoTitle: WIN GAMES with the Nimzo-Indian Defense!
idea: A different plan against Qc2: knight to c6 and pawn to d6 to prepare ...e5 (often after ...Re8), building toward the centre instead of fianchettoing.
note: White's Nf3/a3 are the masters' moves; the ...Nc6/...d6/...e5 plan is from the video.

name: Nimzo vs 4.f3: ...d5 and ...c5
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 f3 d5 a3 Bxc3+ bxc3 c5
videoTitle: WIN GAMES with the Nimzo-Indian Defense!
idea: Against f3 (preparing e4) there is no time for ...b6. Black strikes the centre with ...d5, takes on c3 when a3 is played, and adds ...c5 to pressure d4.
note: Video: after ...d5 the main line is a3, take, then ...c5.

name: Nimzo vs 4.a3: take, ...c5 and target c4
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 a3 Bxc3+ bxc3 c5 e3 b6
videoTitle: WIN GAMES with the Nimzo-Indian Defense!
idea: With the pawns doubled at once, Black keeps the b6/b7 setup in mind but the key lever is ...c5: it hits the clumsy c4 pawn and prepares to open the c-file against it.
note: White's e3 and Black's ...b6 are the masters' most-played; the ...c5 plan is from the video.

name: Queen's Indian fusion: 3.Nf3 b6 4.Nc3 Bb4
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 Nc3 Bb4
videoTitle: WIN GAMES with the Nimzo-Indian Defense!
idea: Against 3.Nf3 play ...b6 first (a Queen's Indian), and if White brings the knight to c3 the bishop goes to b4 anyway, steering back toward the same Nimzo plan of trading on c3 and using e4.

name: vs 2.Bf4: ...e6, ...c5 and ...Qb6 before ...d5
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 e6 e3 c5 c3 Qb6
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: Holding back ...d5 keeps options open: ...c5 is the best lever against the London, and the queen can hit b2 from b6 right away, which is why strong London players prefer Nd2 over an early c3.
note: From Levy's description of his own repertoire vs the London.

name: London: ...cxd4 and ...Nh5 to hunt the bishop
moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nh5 Be3
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: An imbalancing try Levy used to play: swap on d4 so the c-file is half-open, then chase the London bishop with ...Nh5 and keep the f- and g-pawns flexible. Strong players learned to step back to e3 and keep things solid, so it is a surprise weapon rather than a refutation.
note: Thin in both databases (0 master games); presented as a past try, not a recommendation.

name: London: ...cxd4 and ...Bf5
moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Bf5
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: The solid option: trade on d4 and develop the light bishop to f5 opposite White's, a symmetrical position that is safe but gives few winning chances.

name: Open Catalan: ...dxc4 and ...Bb4+ with ...a5
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3 dxc4 Bg2 Bb4+ Bd2 a5
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: Levy's own choice against the Catalan: take the c4 pawn at once, check from b4 so White's bishop comes to d2, and support the b4 bishop with ...a5 while eyeing ...c5. Black hangs on to the pawn for now and makes White prove the g2 bishop's pressure.

name: Open Catalan: check, then back to e7
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3 dxc4 Bg2 Bb4+ Bd2 Be7
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: Instead of trading on d2, the bishop gives the check and steps back to e7, arguing that White's d2 bishop is now a little offside.

name: Closed Catalan: take on c4 after castling, ...a6 and ...Bd7
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O dxc4 Qc2 a6 a4 Bd7
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: The main-line approach: develop and castle first, only then take on c4. When the queen comes to c2, ...a6 threatens ...b5, White stops it with a4, and Black walks the light bishop toward the long diagonal (d7, c6) to fight the g2 bishop.

name: Catalan with a Stonewall twist: ...Ne4 and ...f5
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O c6 Qc2 Ne4 Nc3 f5
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: Black clogs the long diagonal with pawns on c6, d5, e6 and a knight on e4 backed by ...f5, so White's Catalan bishop has nowhere to bite. The engine dislikes the structure slightly, but it throws Catalan players off their plan.

name: Anti-Catalan: ...b5 when c4 is delayed
moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 e6 g3 b5 Bg2 Bb7
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: If White fianchettoes before playing c4, Black grabs queenside space with ...b5 and puts the bishop on b7 to contest the long diagonal, avoiding the main Catalan at the cost of an unbalanced game.

name: Englund: 3...Qe7 tabiya
moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7
videoTitle: WIN IN 8 MOVES: The Englund Gambit
idea: Black gives the e-pawn at once and sets about winning it back: the knight and the queen both attack e5, and the queen on e7 also prepares the ...Qb4+ check that sets every trap in this opening.

name: Englund Trap: mate on c1 in eight
moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Bc3 Bb4 Qd2 Bxc3 Qxc3 Qc1#
videoTitle: WIN IN 8 MOVES: The Englund Gambit
idea: The natural Bf4 lets the queen check, then take b2 hitting the a1 rook. When White defends with Bc3, the pin ...Bb4 means the queen cannot be taken; after the trade on c3 the queen drops into c1 for mate.
note: ends in mate; database counts are for the position before the mating move

name: Englund: 5.Nbd2 drops the f4 bishop
moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Nbd2 Qxf4
videoTitle: WIN IN 8 MOVES: The Englund Gambit
idea: Blocking the check with the queen's knight leaves the bishop on f4 with no defender, and the queen simply takes it.

name: Englund: best play to 10...Kd8
moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Nc3 Bb4 Rb1 Qa3 Nd5 Ba5 Rb5 Bxd2+ Qxd2 Kd8
videoTitle: WIN IN 8 MOVES: The Englund Gambit
idea: The critical line. After Nc3 the bishop pins the knight, White must find Rb1, then Nd5 hits c7 and Rb5 hits the a5 bishop. Black trades on d2 and walks the king to d8 to cover c7 — objectively White is better, but White has to know every move.
note: Video gives the moves through Rb5 and the king to d8; ...Bxd2+ Qxd2 is the amateur database's most-played route there.

name: Englund: queen sacrifice on c3
moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Nc3 Bb4 Rb1 Qxc3 Bxc3 Bxc3+ Nd2 Nxe5
videoTitle: WIN IN 8 MOVES: The Englund Gambit
idea: Black gives the queen for two minor pieces and the e5 pawn. The bishop on c3 pins the d2 knight, so it can't move without allowing a check, and White finds it surprisingly hard to make use of the queen.

name: Englund: 6...Nb4 and the a2 grab
moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Nc3 Nb4 Rc1 Nxa2 Nxa2 Qxa2
videoTitle: WIN IN 8 MOVES: The Englund Gambit
idea: The tricky knight jump hits c2. If White guards with the rook and forgets a2, Black trades on a2 and gets out with an extra pawn; the computer prefers defending with the d4 knight, which is why ...Bb4 is the main recommendation.

name: Englund: f-pawn gambit 4...f6
moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 f6 exf6 Qxf6
videoTitle: WIN IN 8 MOVES: The Englund Gambit
idea: An extra layer for players who want to avoid the theory: give a second pawn, recapture with the queen to hit the f4 bishop and b2, then castle long and play for a lead in development.
